items.rationale: Glitch, who most wants to stay on Rogue's good side, gets a mild public telling-off that nudges his standing with her without changing anything.
Glitch learns he was making a nuisance of himself to the regulars, a small social misstep easily corrected.
Glitch, hunted by Halvorsen with nowhere else to go, is thrown out of his only hiding place tonight just as the retrieval crew is asking about his face.
Rogue, 1,500 short on a Kessler debt that could put her in the canal, is offered stock worth more than the 800 owed, a real if partial help toward the gap.
Rogue's tenant yielding his best stock on demand confirms her control over him, a minor gain in dominance.
Glitch sees his closest friend Mux's overdue rent settled so he keeps his stall, at the cost of Mux's best stock.
Mux, one missed month from losing the stall that is his whole living and home with his daughter, is declared paid up and keeps it.
Rogue hears a public grumble about her bar from her tenant, a small dent in the image her standing rests on.
Rogue's tenant tells the whole room that Vance has taken the next two blocks and she is losing her grip, voicing the exact belief that would let her rival move in.
Glitch watches his friend Mux openly defy and insult the landlord who can take his stall, putting Mux at real risk.
Glitch's protection rests on Rogue's grip on the street, and hearing it publicly questioned unsettles his footing somewhat.
Glitch, who missed the money his sister Pix depends on, learns she got a food parcel, a real but temporary relief.
Glitch learns his dependent sister's rent is paid for six months, securing her home for half a year though it is charged against his future cut.
Mux gets a customer's thanks for a working deck, a small routine confirmation of his skill.
Mux hears he revived a deck three shops had scrapped and that word of it has spread across the grid, a major boost to the name he is proud of.
Mux, behind on rent, hears three crews are bringing him rigs, promised business that could help keep the stall.
Mux, already two months behind at 400, faces a ten-eddy rent rise, an annoyance that barely changes his position.
Rogue's tenant accepts a ten-eddy rent rise without a fight, a barely noticeable assertion of control.
Mux loses the right to make any sizable sale in his own stall without Rogue's approval, a lasting curb on running his own business.
Mux learns the building is being sold and his stall, his whole living and the room he lives in, will be gone at month's end.
Mux learns his nine-year-old daughter Tess will lose the home above the stall at the end of the month.
Rogue hears of a cop drone that is probably nothing, a passing note on a street she runs.
Rogue, 1,500 short, learns Kessler's 4,000 is due tonight rather than in three days, and those who miss Kessler's dates end up in the canal.
Rogue is told Kessler will run his packages through her grid with no questions, making the street she controls answer to him.
Rogue loses say over what moves through her own grid as part of a deal she cannot refuse.
Glitch, whose shelter Rogue is openly weighing, gets no answer to his only peace offering, leaving his place in doubt.
Mux, short again with one more missed month costing him the stall, has his only means of paying refused, putting his living and home in jeopardy.
Rogue's order banishing Glitch from her bar is obeyed at once, a small confirmation of her authority.
Glitch is told which stool to take, a trivial limit on his choice.
Glitch loses the right to choose his own jobs and half of every score from now on, a lasting loss of control over his work.
Glitch, with nowhere else to hide, is told he can stay on in Rogue's back room.
Mux, whose reputation is how he gets customers, is publicly blamed by the street's fixer for a deck that fried a kid's jack.
Mux, behind on rent with the stall as his whole living, has the street's fixer tell people not to buy from him.
Rogue is publicly toasted for landing a contract nobody else could touch, real recognition by the standards of her street.
Rogue hears herself hailed in the room as the best fixer on the east side, reinforcing the belief her hold on the street rests on.
Glitch, late with Rogue's cut and with only 60 eddies, has his stopgap refused and stays in arrears with the woman sheltering him.
Glitch hears that Rogue, who shelters him, has a 20,000 offer from the people hunting him to kill him and is asking why she shouldn't take it.
Mux hears Rogue weigh selling his closest friend Glitch to the people hunting him for 20,000.
Glitch, facing Rogue's question about selling him to Halvorsen, has his last offering refused, so his plea for his life has not landed.
Mux hears a public jab that his jukebox fix failed, a minor knock to his craftsman's pride.
Mux, proud of bringing any deck back, is publicly declared to have killed every deck he touched this month.
Mux, behind on rent and living off the stall, has the street's fixer tell everyone, including Kiroshi's runners, to take their gear elsewhere.
Glitch watches his closest friend Mux's name and living publicly destroyed by the fixer who controls the street.
Rogue's errand is done as asked, a routine instance of being obeyed.
Rogue's tenant publicly announces he is moving to her rival Vance and that Vance treats people better, a direct public sign of her slipping grip.
Rogue faces losing a tenant who owes her back rent and a visible crack in the stability of her street.
Rogue publicly orders her defecting tenant back to his stall and he goes, reasserting control in front of the room.
Glitch hears his friend Mux burned his thumb again, a trivial everyday hurt.
Glitch learns his closest friend had two fingers broken protecting him and the men will return.
Glitch learns his hunters have found the stall where he sleeps and are coming back.
Mux, 800 behind, gets five eddies off this month, barely a dent in what he owes.
Mux is freed to set his own prices without Rogue checking his books, a real gain in running his own business.
Mux has all his back rent forgiven and the stall that is his living and his daughter's home guaranteed as long as Rogue runs the grid.
Mux is credited by the fixer with keeping Glitch's deck alive through the Halvorsen trace, recognition of his skill that paid off.
Rogue learns Halvorsen may have touched a trace on her line, a real worry even if Glitch thinks he cut it in time.
Rogue learns Halvorsen has traced her bar's address and will be there tonight, putting her bar and herself in danger.
Rogue is publicly toasted for making Kessler drop his interest, real recognition of a hard win.
Rogue hears the room told nobody else could make Kessler blink, shoring up her standing as the street's fixer.
Mux gets a free drink on the house, a small pleasure.
Glitch loses all freedom to pick his own work and prices, bound to run only Rogue's jobs from now on.
Rogue is told Kessler will take her bar unless she meets him alone at midnight, putting the bar and her own safety on the line.
Rogue is summoned on Kessler's terms with no choice of time, place or company.
Glitch, just bound to run only Rogue's jobs, is offered the means to run his own rig independently, though only as an offer.
Glitch gains a possible power source of his own, a modest hedge given that going around Rogue could also cost him her favour.
Mux sees his closest friend accept his best stock and with it a way out from under Rogue's control.
